models.collectorNote: Judges and Ram Air IV cars are blue-chip muscle; protect-o-plate and build-sheet documentation separate the money cars from the clones. The 2004–06 cars are the sleeper performance buy.

generations.name: GTO (first era)
generations.note: Tri-power 389s made up to 360 hp; by 1967 the 400 had arrived with Ram Air options. The 1966 car is the volume icon, nearly 97,000 sold that year.

generations.name: GTO / The Judge
generations.note: The coke-bottle A-body, Endura nose, and from 1969 The Judge in Carousel Red. Ram Air IV 400s rated 370 hp closed the era before insurance and emissions closed the market.

generations.name: GTO (Holden-built)
generations.note: A Monaro in Pontiac dress, built in Australia: LS1 then 400 hp LS2, six-speed manual available, and a chassis far better than the badge's seventies reputation suggested.

models.intro: The original muscle car: John DeLorean's team slipped a 389 big-block into a mid-size Tempest in 1964 and the era began. Judge, Ram Air, a wilderness decade, and a final Australian-built encore in 2004.

models.collectorNote: SD-455s and first-gen Trans Ams are the summit; Bandit-spec Special Editions are the market's mood ring. WS6 LS1 cars remain the performance-per-dollar pick.

generations.name: Firebird (first generation)
generations.note: Shared Camaro bones, Pontiac attitude: the 400 Ram Air cars made up to 335 hp and the 1969 Trans Am, just 697 built, started the legend.

generations.name: Firebird / Trans Am (second generation)
generations.note: The long gen: 455 Super Duty (1973–74) is the last true muscle peak, the 1977 black-and-gold Special Edition became the Bandit car, and turbos arrived for 1980. Sales peaked with the film.

generations.name: Firebird / Trans Am (fourth generation)
generations.note: LT1 then LS1 power; the WS6 Ram Air package took the final cars to 320 hp with handling to match. The 2002 Collector Edition closed the line.

models.intro: Pontiac's F-body, four generations deep: Ram Air originals, the SD-455, the Bandit phenomenon, Knight Rider, and a final LS1 WS6 that was a Corvette in a tuxedo t-shirt.

generations.name: Grand Prix (first generation)
generations.note: The 1962 original set the formula: full-size body, sports-car cockpit. The 421 HO reached 376 hp, serious pace in a luxury coupe.

generations.name: Grand Prix GTP
generations.note: The W-body reinvention: a supercharged 3800 V6 at 240 hp in a wide-track sedan and coupe that outsold expectations and defined Pontiac's last volume decade.

models.intro: Pontiac's personal-luxury nameplate for 46 years: born as a full-size performance coupe with bucket seats and a 421 option, ending as a supercharged front-drive sedan, the GXP even got a V8.

models.collectorNote: The 1957 fuelie convertibles are the blue-chip cars; the rest of the line is affordable full-size Americana. Documentation of the injection system matters.

generations.name: Bonneville (fuel-injected debut)
generations.note: The 1957 car's Rochester fuel injection on the 347 V8 was headline tech, rating around 300 hp; only 630 convertibles were built. The nameplate then ran as Pontiac's flagship until 2005.

models.intro: Named for the salt flats and launched as a fuel-injected convertible flagship in 1957, every first-year car was a convertible, and 'fuel injection' was Pontiac announcing it had arrived as a performance brand.

models.collectorNote: 1988 GTs are the collector spec and still cheap; the kit-car donor history means original unmodified cars are the rarity. Buy the cleanest chassis, not the lowest miles.

generations.name: Fiero / Fiero GT
generations.note: Iron Duke four or 2.8 V6; the GT's 140 hp in a light mid-engine chassis made the case the launch car hadn't. Nearly 370,000 built across five years.

models.intro: America's mid-engine commuter car that became a sports car just in time to be cancelled: plastic panels on a spaceframe, a V6 GT by 1985, and a proper fastback for 1986. The 1988 suspension, finally all Pontiac's own design, was the best and the last.

models.collectorNote: Coupes first, GXPs second, manuals over automatics throughout. The last Pontiac halo car has a floor under it and a story that only gets better.

generations.name: Solstice / GXP
generations.note: The GXP's direct-injected 2.0 turbo made 260 hp, the highest specific output GM had then produced. Just 1,266 coupes were built before the marque closed, making them instant collectibles.

models.intro: Bob Lutz's back-to-basics roadster and Pontiac's last halo: a concept car (2002) willed into production, outselling the MX-5 in its first year, with the turbo GXP and a rare targa coupe as the collector endings.
